title: Where AI helped on my first Unity game, and where I still had to put it on a phone
author: TidyShuffle
selftext:
Tidy Shuffle is my first game. It’s a Unity puzzle for Android where you sort a pile of everyday objects into boxes. I used Claude Code for Unity implementation and technical tests, and Codex for things like asset work and visual checks. I also used generated art and audio. I made the calls about what felt right to play.



One example: I wanted to pan the hallway sideways from the normal zoom level so it felt like there was more room to look around. On my old Galaxy A5, the first wider version had a thin bright seam where the side art met the original background. We traced it to the edge pixels and texture filtering. We checked the fix on the phone, including zooming in. The boxes stay still while the room moves. That little detail mattered more to me than getting the camera code working on the first try.



The other big one was sorting categories. A blue book cover looked like a bag at phone size. The item name looked fine in the data. Seeing the actual piece at the size you’d tap it made the problem obvious. That changed what I ask the tools to check: look at the actual board and the boxes together.



Even with AI it was a ridiculous amount of work, especially getting it out the door. I’d be curious what other people here still insist on checking by hand after an AI-assisted build.



If you want to try it, it’s free on Android with ads and an optional purchase: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cardeastudios.tidyshuffle&utm\_source=reddit&utm\_campaign=aigamedev\_workflow](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cardeastudios.tidyshuffle&utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=aigamedev_workflow)
